translationRepairs: Lang Tan, of the Guwalgiya clan, was a Manchu of the Plain White Banner and the son of Grand Secretary Wu Bai.
Lang Tan, of the Guwalgiya clan, was a Manchu of the Plain White Banner and the son of Minister of the Imperial Household Wu Bai.
內大臣 is the Minister of the Imperial Household (chamberlain), not Grand Secretary (大學士).
Lang Tan, of the Guwalgiya clan, was a Manchu of the Plain White Banner and the son of Grand Secretary Wu Bai.
Lang Tan, of the Guwalgiya clan, was a Manchu of the Plain White Banner and the son of Minister of the Imperial Household Wu Bai.
Same 內大臣 mistranslation as Grand Secretary in the literal English.
In Shunzhi 8 (1651), when Wu Bai was condemned for siding with Grand Secretary Losi and others, Lang Tan was stripped of his post as well.
In Shunzhi 8 (1651), when Wu Bai was condemned for siding with Minister of the Imperial Household Losi and others, Lang Tan was stripped of his post as well.
內大臣洛什 should not be rendered Grand Secretary.

In Kangxi 28 (1689) Grand Secretary Songgotu met Russian envoys led by Fyodor at Nerchinsk to fix the border; Lang Tan joined the talks, after which the Russian posts were dismantled and the garrisons withdrawn.

In Kangxi 28 (1689) Minister of the Imperial Household Songgotu met Russian envoys led by Fyodor at Nerchinsk to fix the border; Lang Tan joined the talks, after which the Russian posts were dismantled and the garrisons withdrawn.
內大臣索額圖 is not Grand Secretary; use Minister of the Imperial Household.
He was soon made chief commandant of the imperial bodyguards and grand secretary, superintendent of the Firearms Brigade, and a grand councillor.
He was soon made chief commandant of the imperial bodyguards (ling shiwei nei dachen), superintendent of the Firearms Brigade, and a grand councillor.
領侍衛內大臣 is a single office, not bodyguard commandant plus a separate grand secretary.
He retained his posts as chief bodyguard commandant, grand secretary, and grand councillor.
He retained his posts as chief commandant of the imperial bodyguards and grand councillor.
領侍衛內大臣 is one office; remove the spurious grand secretary.
Peng Chun, of the Donggo clan, was a Manchu of the Plain Red Banner and a fourth-generation descendant of Hešeri.
Peng Chun, of the Donggo clan, was a Manchu of the Plain Red Banner and a fourth-generation descendant of He Heli.
何和禮 is He Heli (Hohoheli), not the Hešeri (赫舍里) clan name.
Peng Chun, of the Donggo clan, was a Manchu of the Plain Red Banner and a fourth-generation descendant of Hešeri.
Peng Chun, of the Donggo clan, was a Manchu of the Plain Red Banner and a fourth-generation descendant of He Heli.
Same Hešeri mistranslation of 何和禮 in the literal English.
Hešeri's son Heshotu was raised to third-rank duke;
He Heli's son Heshotu was raised to third-rank duke;
何和禮 should be He Heli, not Hešeri.
His son Zengshou inherited as third-rank duke.
His son Zengshou succeeded by a change of inheritance as third-rank duke.
Chinese 改襲 means the hereditary rank was altered, not simple unchanged succession.
In Kangxi 16 (1677) the Kangxi Emperor sent Grand Secretary Aisin Gioro Wumuna and others to worship at Mount Changbai; at Jilin they needed a guide who knew the way.
In Kangxi 16 (1677) the Kangxi Emperor sent Grand Minister of the Imperial Household Aisin Gioro Wumuna and others to worship at Mount Changbai; at Jilin they needed a guide who knew the way.
內大臣 is Grand Minister of the Imperial Household, not Grand Secretary (大學士).

In the sixteenth year of Kangxi the Sacred Ancestor sent Grand Secretary Aisin Gioro Wumuna and others to pay homage at Mount Changbai; when they reached Jilin they wished to find someone who knew the route to guide them.

In the sixteenth year of Kangxi the Sacred Ancestor sent Grand Minister of the Imperial Household Aisin Gioro Wumuna and others to pay homage at Mount Changbai; when they reached Jilin they wished to find someone who knew the route to guide them.
內大臣 is mistranslated as Grand Secretary.
In Kangxi 28 (1689), when Russian envoys led by Fyodor reached Nerchinsk, Grand Secretary Songgotu was sent to meet them with fifteen hundred Heilongjiang troops as guard.
In Kangxi 28 (1689), when Russian envoys led by Fyodor reached Nerchinsk, Grand Minister of the Imperial Household Songgotu was sent to meet them with fifteen hundred Heilongjiang troops as guard.
內大臣索額圖 is Grand Minister of the Imperial Household, not Grand Secretary.

In the twenty-eighth year the Russian envoys Feodor and others arrived at Nerchinsk; Grand Secretary Songgotu and others were ordered to meet them, and fifteen hundred Heilongjiang troops were sent as escort.

In the twenty-eighth year the Russian envoys Feodor and others arrived at Nerchinsk; Grand Minister of the Imperial Household Songgotu and others were ordered to meet them, and fifteen hundred Heilongjiang troops were sent as escort.
內大臣 is mistranslated as Grand Secretary.
In Kangxi 29 (1690) Sa Bu Su came to court, received lavish gifts, and was seated in the grand secretary rank.
In Kangxi 29 (1690) Sa Bu Su came to court, received lavish gifts, and was seated in the rank of the Grand Ministers of the Imperial Household.
內大臣班 is the Imperial Household chamberlain seating rank, not grand secretary rank.
In the twenty-ninth year Sa Bu Su came to audience; generous gifts were bestowed and he was ordered to sit in the grand secretary rank.
In the twenty-ninth year Sa Bu Su came to audience; generous gifts were bestowed and he was ordered to sit in the rank of the Grand Ministers of the Imperial Household.
內大臣班 does not mean grand secretary rank.

In Kangxi 35 (1696) the emperor campaigned in person from Dushikou on the center route while Grand General Fiyanggū marched from Guihua on the west; Sa Bu Su was to block the east with Shengjing, Ningguta, and Khorchin troops advancing from Suoyorji Mountain on schedule.

In Kangxi 35 (1696) the emperor personally campaigned against Galdan from Dushikou on the center route while Grand General Fiyanggū marched from Guihua on the west; Sa Bu Su was to block the east with Shengjing, Ningguta, and Khorchin troops advancing from Suoyorji Mountain on schedule.
Idiomatic English omits 噶爾丹, the stated campaign target present in the Chinese and literal.
With Grand Secretary Kadai he proclaimed imperial prohibitions to the outer Khorchin banners.
With Inner Minister Kadai he proclaimed imperial prohibitions to the outer Khorchin banners.
內大臣 is Inner Minister / Grand Minister of the Household, not Grand Secretary (大學士).
Together with Grand Secretary Kadai he went to the outer Khorchin vassals to proclaim prohibitions.
Together with Inner Minister Kadai he went to the outer Khorchin vassals to proclaim prohibitions.
內大臣 is Inner Minister / Grand Minister of the Household, not Grand Secretary (大學士).
The emperor recalled that Sa Bu Su had once urged removing Governor Cai Yurong from the twelve forts and that the change had worked well;
The emperor recalled that Sa Bu Su had once memorialized to dismiss Governor Cai Yurong from managing the twelve forts and that the change had worked well;
革任…經理 means dismiss from the managing post, not merely remove him from the forts as a place.

In the twenty-ninth year Galdan raided the Khalkha; Ma La was ordered, together with Lieutenant-General Ehena, Vanguard Commander Shuonai, and others, to lead troops against him and was granted an imperial groom and horse for the journey.

In the twenty-ninth year Galdan raided the Khalkha; Ma La was ordered, together with Lieutenant-General Ehena, Vanguard Commander Shuonai, and others, to lead troops against him and was granted horses from the imperial stables for the journey.
內廝馬 means horses from the imperial stables (內廝), not an imperial groom plus a horse.
In Kangxi 32 (1693) Dzungar Khoshut taiji Batur Erkejin surrendered; the emperor distrusted them and ordered Ma La to move them inland and prevent escape.
In Kangxi 32 (1693) Dzungar Khoshut taiji Batur Erkejin came to surrender; the emperor considered his people not yet trustworthy and ordered Ma La to move them inland and prevent escape.
Chinese 來降 and 其人未可信 refer to Batur coming to surrender and his people not yet being trustworthy; idiomatic collapses this and pluralizes distrust without the people nuance.
